text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Ang Wei Neng –   42 To ask the Minister for Transport whether Singapore is considering accelerating Vaccinated Travel Lane (VTL) arrangements with more territories, especially those with lower COVID-19 infection rates such as Australia, China, Hong Kong and New Zealand.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry will consider increasing the quota for passengers from Vaccinated Travel Lane (VTL) flights given that VTL flights are from countries with similar risks and that the adult passengers are already vaccinated and tested multiple times prior to entry.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: My reply would take a little bit longer than the allotted time.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I also would like to address similar questions on this subject that have been filed by Mr Saktiandi Supaat1, Mr Louis Chua2, Mr Gerald Giam3, Mr Shawn Huang4 and Mr Dennis5 Tan for subsequent Sittings.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I want to start by taking stock of where we are in terms of border reopening.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Members would be aware that MOH has established a risk-based categorisation of countries and regions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This framework is based on its public health assessment of a country or region’s COVID-19 situation, including its infection rate and vaccination coverage.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Countries and regions in Category I are of the lowest risk.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Currently, this includes Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These are countries and regions which continue to adopt a "zero-COVID" approach, and which therefore continue to have very low COVID-19 incidence rates.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To Mr Ang Wei Neng’s question, we have already opened our borders to all travellers from these countries unilaterally.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They can enter Singapore quarantine-free and only need to undergo an on-arrival PCR test.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To Mr Gerald Giam’s question, we do not require the visitors who arrive from these Category I countries and regions to be vaccinated.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Countries and regions in Category II are of a similar incidence rate to Singapore or lower.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Since 8 September 2020, we have reopened to vaccinated travellers from some of these countries in a cautious and calibrated manner through the Vaccinated Travel Lanes (VTLs).

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We started the VTL scheme with two countries, namely Brunei Darussalam and Germany, and have since extended it to eight others.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have also announced the commencement of VTLs with Australia and Switzerland from 8 November, and with the Republic of Korea from 15 November.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In total, we have launched VTLs with 13 countries, which is a fraction of the countries that Changi Airport was connected to pre-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Collectively, they accounted for about 15% of Changi’s annual passenger arrivals pre-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Louis Chua have asked about the quota and designated flights for the VTLs, and how these are distributed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We set an overall quota for the VTL scheme as a safeguard to manage the public health risk.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The quota is allocated to airlines operating flights to and from VTL countries based on the plans they submit.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The allocation for each country and airline can vary based on demand, but the total will be kept within the overall quota.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The airlines can only carry eligible passengers on the designated VTL flights.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) monitors the airlines closely to ensure their adherence to the stipulated measures and allocated quota.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will monitor the incidence rate and the proportion of imported cases closely, review the demand, before deciding on any further increases in the quotas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Shawn Hwang and Mr Dennis Tan have asked about our plans to extend the VTLs to more countries and our criteria for doing so.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are in discussions with several partners, including our regional neighbours, to reopen safely to each other.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We hope to conclude these discussions soon and restore our connectivity with them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have therefore expanded the VTL scheme step-by-step, informed by the public health assessment of the country's or region’s COVID-19 situation, and also the operational risks and implications.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This includes whether key safeguards under the VTL scheme can be effectively implemented, such as whether travellers from the VTL countries can present digitally verifiable and authenticated proof of vaccination as a precondition for entry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We work closely with MOH to regularly review safeguards such as the testing protocols based on the latest scientific evidence and testing technology.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Even as we seek to reopen our border and restore connectivity with the rest of the world, safeguarding public health is our utmost priority.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Saktiandi has asked whether the VTL approach is transitory and what my Ministry’s plans are for reopening our borders thereafter.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will progressively expand the scheme as we gain experience and confidence in reopening our borders safely.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ultimately, our goal is to restore safe two-way quarantine-free travel with countries and regions from around the world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As part of "Living with COVID-19", we must be resolute and press on with the reopening of our borders, while staying vigilant with the essential public health safeguards.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is crucial to rebuilding and reclaiming our status as an international aviation hub.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ministerial Statement on behalf of the Minister for Health.
